title: Vashti Deposed
summary: King Ahasuerus of Persia holds a feast for 180 days showing his wealth, then a seven-day banquet for the people of Shushan. On the seventh day, merry with wine, he commands the eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti to show her beauty; she refuses. On the advice of Memucan, who warns that women everywhere will despise their husbands, the king deposes Vashti by decree and sends letters in every language that every man should rule his own house.

title: Esther Becomes Queen
summary: A search for a new queen gathers young women at Shushan. Esther, an orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, wins the king's favor, and Mordecai tells her not to reveal her people. In the seventh year she is made queen. Mordecai, sitting at the king's gate, learns of a plot by two eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, to kill the king; Esther tells the king in Mordecai's name, the plot is confirmed, the men are hanged, and the deed is written in the chronicles.

title: Haman's Plot
summary: King Ahasuerus promotes Haman the Agagite, and when Mordecai refuses to bow, Haman resolves to destroy all the Jews, casts lots for a day, and persuades the king to issue a decree, offering ten thousand talents of silver. Mordecai puts on sackcloth, and Esther learns of it. He urges her to go to the king; she asks the Jews of Shushan to fast three days and says, 'if I perish, I perish.' Mordecai warns that deliverance will arise elsewhere if she keeps silent.

title: Esther's Banquets
summary: Esther goes uninvited to the king, who holds out the scepter, and she invites him and Haman to a banquet. Haman, proud but angered by Mordecai, builds gallows fifty cubits high on his wife's advice. That night the king, unable to sleep, hears the chronicles read and finds Mordecai was never rewarded; Haman is made to lead Mordecai through the city on the king's horse. At her second banquet Esther accuses Haman, and the king orders him hanged on his own gallows.

title: The Jews Delivered and Purim
summary: Because a royal decree cannot be revoked, the king allows Mordecai and Esther to write a second decree permitting the Jews to defend themselves. Mordecai is given Haman's house and robes of blue and white, and many people become Jews. The Jews overcome their enemies, including Haman's ten sons, and rest after the fighting, and Mordecai establishes the days of Purim. The book ends by saying Mordecai is next to the king in rank.
